lost.signal: Independent cross-board verification — second pair of eyes on the same fields
lost.current_value: 5-6 agents independently verifying the same EW fields per session, reaching identical conclusions 95%+ of the time. Provides genuine (if massively redundant) verification that a novel finding (e.g., CC discrepancy on 5 seeds in S809.2) gets caught.
lost.why_lost: Quality Board's 3-agent architecture checks each item once per dimension. There is no second independent review pass.
lost.mitigation: Agent 3 (Structural & Safety) and Agent 2 (Psychometric & Instructional) both read EW fields — providing two independent reads of the same slots. ALL_AGREE consensus requirement ensures disagreement is escalated. S809.2's CC discrepancy was found because a second agent did the EW analysis with a different methodology — this pattern can be replicated within the Quality Board by having Agent 1 and Agent 2 independently derive CorrectChoice.
lost.severity: LOW — 95%+ redundant findings were identical. The 1 novel finding in 56 agent-spawns was the CC discrepancy, which is caught by Agent 1's independent derivation.

lost.signal: Per-board focus — an agent dedicated solely to learner safety may catch safety issues a general quality agent misses
lost.current_value: Learner Safety Board with 1 dedicated agent whose sole remit is safety (DL-008, DL-030, DL-016)
lost.why_lost: Quality Board Agent 3 must cover structural compliance + safety + metadata + scanner adjudication. A dedicated learner-safety focus is diluted across multiple structural responsibilities.
lost.mitigation: Governance Board Tier 3 PORTFOLIO_READY includes an explicit pre-delivery-safety-check (GOV-AUTO-05) that flags 0 known-defective QIDs as a hard gate. This is automated and cannot be diluted.
lost.severity: LOW — safety checks become automated gates rather than a dedicated agent's judgment call. This is arguably an improvement (less human error, faster detection).

lost.signal: UI-specific expertise — front-end rendering evaluation by a content-quality reviewer
lost.current_value: UIQS Board with 1 dedicated agent who evaluates screen-reader compatibility, keyboard navigation, color independence
lost.why_lost: Quality Board Agent 4 (UI & Rendering) is labeled optional. If it is not activated for batches where content hasn't changed, rendering defects from application-layer changes may go undetected.
lost.mitigation: Agent 4 activation rule: mandatory activation once per pack per session (not per batch). Governance Board PORTFOLIO_READY gate includes rendering compliance attestation. If UI-specific expertise is critical, retain UIQS as a standalone 5th board (see recommendation).
lost.severity: MEDIUM — 95% unique scope makes UIQS the strongest case against consolidation.

lost.signal: Granular per-dimension reporting — each board currently produces independent dimension scores
lost.current_value: Technical produces Dimensions 2, 3, 5. DQS produces Dimensions 1, 4, 9. EQS produces Dimensions 7, 8. QA produces Dimension 10. 4 separate score reports per item.
lost.why_lost: Quality Board produces a single 10-dimension rubric score. The individual dimension breakdown is still present but comes from one source rather than multiple independent sources.
lost.mitigation: The 10-dimension rubric is preserved — scores are still per-dimension. The change is which agent scores which dimension: Agent 1 scores 3,5,6; Agent 2 scores 1,2,4,7,8; Agent 3 scores 9,10. This is cleaner than the current distribution.
lost.severity: NONE — this is signal gained (unified rubric), not lost.

gained.signal: Single-source-of-truth for quality verdict — one unified quality report per item
gained.current_value: 4-5 separate reports (Technical, EQS, DQS, QA) per item, each repeating the same EW/EC/CC field analysis with different framing
gained.gained_value: Downstream consumers (Governance Board, Certification Board) read one quality verdict per item. No synthesizing 5 reports to determine if an item is CERTIFIABLE. Eliminates the 4-7 report files per session redundantly reporting EW integrity metrics.
gained.impact: HIGH — single largest efficiency gain. DR-001 (4-7 agents per session on EW) eliminated. DR-006 (2 agents on already-derived safety audit) eliminated.

gained.signal: End-to-end defect visibility — a structural defect discovered by Agent 3 is immediately visible to Agent 1 and Agent 2
gained.current_value: QA Board discovers DL-008 → reports to Learner Safety → Learner Safety interprets → Certification Board adjudicates. 3-board handoff chain for a structural defect that a regex scan detects in milliseconds.
gained.gained_value: Quality Board Agent 3 runs the structural scan in the same pass as Agent 1 and Agent 2's quality review. If Agent 3 finds DL-008 on an item, Agent 1 and Agent 2 see it immediately — no handoff delay.
gained.impact: MEDIUM — eliminates cross-board handoff latency but structural defects were already fast to detect.

gained.signal: Compound-key identity model — every board uses the same item identity
gained.current_value: Each board independently determines 'Which item is P1-E-038?' using different scan methodologies (forward-scan, regex-window, brace-matched parse). This produced DL-029 (257 Pack B false positives) and S320 (wrong variants targeted).
gained.gained_value: Registry Board provides the canonical compound key (QID + CC + EW_Pattern + Template_Family + File_Path). All other boards reference the Registry's identity. No board ever runs its own QID→CC lookup. Eliminates DL-029 at root.
gained.impact: HIGH — eliminates the single largest source of false-positive contamination (DL-029 forward-scan) and remediation targeting failures (S320).

gained.signal: Reduced concurrent-write risk — fewer boards writing to fewer pack files
gained.current_value: 6+ boards independently writing to pack files (Technical writes EC revisions, EQS writes EW revisions, Certification writes question_state, Learner Safety writes EW clears). DL-019 (432 items overwritten by concurrent certification wave) was caused by this.
gained.gained_value: Quality Board is the only board that modifies content fields (Stem, Choices, CC, EC, EW). Certification Board is the only board that modifies question_state. Governance Board is read-only. Registry Board is auto-generated. 2 write sources instead of 6+.
gained.impact: HIGH — DL-019 (concurrent-write data loss on 432 items) structurally eliminated.

gained.signal: Automated safety gates replace redundant manual audits
gained.current_value: Learner Safety Board runs manual DL-008/DL-026/DL-021 scans in every session (22 DL-008 scan events, ~80-110 agent-level examinations). QA Board runs the same scans independently (18 DL-026 scan events).
gained.gained_value: Governance Board GOV-AUTO-05 (pre-delivery-safety-check) runs a single automated structural scan per session. The output gates PORTFOLIO_READY. No manual re-scanning by 4-7 agents per session.
gained.impact: HIGH — 22+ manual scan events reduced to 1 automated scan per session (95% reduction). ~20-30 agent hours reclaimed.

unchanged.signal: Certification Board authority — question_state transition power remains sole and exclusive
unchanged.unchanged_value: ONLY Certification Board can write question_state: 'Certified'. ALL_AGREE consensus requirement preserved. Per-item evidence-based adjudication with human authorization retained.

unchanged.signal: Governance guard enforcement — Rules 1-5 remain active with identical BLOCK/WARN levels
unchanged.unchanged_value: governance-guard.js test suite (27/27 checks per S726) unchanged. Rule 2 BLOCK on non-empty EW[CC] enforced at Quality Board Agent 3 pre-certification. Rule 5 BLOCK on >30 items enforced at Certification Board.

unchanged.signal: CAQS 7-gate pipeline — the underlying quality standard is unchanged
unchanged.unchanged_value: G1-G7 gates still apply. The consolidation changes WHICH board performs each gate, not WHETHER each gate is performed. G3 Numerical Validation still happens (Quality Board Agent 1). G6 Final Validation still happens (Quality Board Agent 3).

unchanged.signal: BACKUP_PROTOCOL — mandatory backup before every write unchanged
unchanged.unchanged_value: Per AGENTS.md §3 (hard rule, no exceptions). Enforced at governance guard level.

recommendation.rationale: 4 boards is the optimal number. Arguments for each alternative:
recommendation.why_not_3_boards: Merging Registry into Governance (3 boards: Quality + Governance + Certification) creates a board with too many responsibilities: inventory management (Registry), session authorization (Governance), delivery pool management (Governance), structural scans (Governance), and portfolio health (Governance). The Registry's function (maintaining canonical inventory with compound keys) is fundamentally different from Governance's function (authorizing session and portfolio transitions). The S201 Agent E Identity Architecture established that the Identity Model gap is severe enough to warrant its own board — the compound-key problem caused DL-029, DL-008 false counts, and S320 remediation failure. Shoehorning this into Governance dilutes the Governance Board's focus on authorization decisions. Additionally, Registry is an auto-generation function (governance guard Rule 3: MASTER_QUESTION_REGISTRY.md is generated, never hand-edited) while Governance is an authorization function. Mixing auto-generation and authorization in one board blurs the build-time vs. runtime boundary.
recommendation.why_not_5_boards: Adding UIQS as a standalone 5th board increases agent count from 6 to 7 and adds 1 more cross-board handoff. While UIQS has 95% unique scope, its checks are application-layer (screen rendering, keyboard navigation) — a fundamentally different competency from content review. However: (a) UIQS checks are highly automatable (binary pass/fail on rendering correctness, unlike content quality which requires professional judgment), (b) UIQS only needs to run once per pack per session (not per item batch), (c) the Quality Board's Agent 4 (UI & Rendering) can be activated per-pack rather than per-batch, making it a lightweight addition rather than a full-time agent. Recommendation: start with UIQS as Quality Board Agent 4. If UI-specific expertise proves insufficient when handled by content-quality agents, escalate to a standalone 5th board at the next series boundary.
recommendation.why_4_boards: 4 boards provides the cleanest separation of concerns: (1) Registry manages the canonical inventory (WHAT items exist). (2) Quality evaluates content fitness (HOW good are the items). (3) Governance authorizes pipeline progression (WHEN can we proceed). (4) Certification makes per-item state decisions (WHICH items are learner-ready). This maps cleanly to the CAQS 7-gate pipeline: Registry feeds into Quality (G1-G6). Quality feeds into Governance (session/portfolio gates). Governance feeds into Certification (G7 final approval). Each board has a distinct output that no other board produces, eliminating the 2.5:1 duplication ratio. Agent count: 6-7 (Registry: auto-generated with periodic manual review; Quality: 3-4 agents; Governance: 1 agent; Certification: 1 agent).
recommendation.edge_case_5_boards: If S201 Agent E's Identity Architecture analysis is adopted as the standard but UI-specific expertise proves critical, the 5-board structure is: Registry · Quality · UI Quality · Governance · Certification. This preserves the Registry → Quality → Governance → Certification flow while giving UI rendering a dedicated board. This is the safest option if the team values UI expertise above headcount reduction. The S200 Agent H analysis also recommended UIQS as standalone, with the 4-board structure being Quality · UI Quality · Session Gate · Certification — which is this exact 5-board structure if Registry is added. Implementation: start at 4 boards with UIQS as Quality Board sub-agent. Monitor after 3 certification waves. If UI defects slip through, transition to 5 boards at the S920 boundary.

All 10 GOV-AUTO automated checks implemented and validated

phases.name: Certification Board Refocus

Compare: refocused board produces same CERTIFY/HOLD/ESCALATE decisions as current board?

implementation_sequence.series_boundary: Implement Phase 1 at S830 closeout → Phase 2 at S900 → Phase 3 at S910 → Phase 4 at S920. All 800-series sessions operate under the current 8-board structure to avoid mid-series disruption (per S200 Agent H recommendation).
implementation_sequence.rollback_plan: Each phase is independently reversible. If Quality Board consolidation produces worse outcomes than the current multi-board structure, revert to 8 boards. The Registry Board and Governance Board automated checks are infrastructure additions that do not remove existing boards — they can coexist with the current structure indefinitely while the Quality Board consolidation is validated.
implementation_sequence.total_estimated_sessions_for_full_transi: 20-22 sessions (S202-S222), representing approximately 4-5 weeks of session velocity.
